findings.title: Cached snapshot may miss changes that don't bump Revision
findings.message: The frame loop now reuses a cached snapshot until `Revision` changes. Exit readiness, Closed status and any other state that can change without bumping the session revision would then go unseen. For example, background job completion or endpoint retirement could leave `ReadyToExit()` stale and the window would never close. This holds only if `SnapshotIfChanged` keys solely on `Revision`.
findings.suggestion: Make sure every field the loop reads (`ReadyToExit`, Closed, job status) changes the revision or a change token that `SnapshotIfChanged` uses. Otherwise, take a fresh snapshot periodically or on shutdown-related events.

findings.title: Contributor validation narrowed to RMS only
findings.message: Previously the whole `Contributors` slice was compared with `reflect.DeepEqual`. Now only each contributor's `RMS` slice is compared. The earlier loop checks ID, ComponentID, Mechanism, Density and Unit against the drives. Any other field that `summarizeNoise` derives (for example a ranking, share or peak) is no longer validated, so a tampered or stale record could pass. The loop also assumes `expected` and `r` have the same number of contributors, with no length check.
findings.suggestion: First check `len(expected.Noise.Contributors) == len(r.Noise.Contributors)`. Then compare each contributor exactly on every non-float field: copy both structs, set `RMS` to nil on the copies, and `DeepEqual` them. Compare only the float fields with the roundoff tolerance.

findings.title: No baseline assertion that unmodified record validates
findings.message: The test only checks that `validateNoiseRecord` returns an error for modified records. It never checks that the unmodified record passes. A validator that always returns an error (for example, because the plan does not match) would make both negative checks pass. The rejections would then prove nothing about detecting material changes.
findings.suggestion: Before mutating, assert that validation of an unmodified clone succeeds, e.g. `if err := validateNoiseRecord(plan, cloneSweepResult(state.DCSweep.Result)); err != nil { t.Fatal(err) }`.

findings.title: Possible index-out-of-range panic building verification preview
findings.message: The verification preview indexes `record.rows[len(record.rows)-1]` and `record.metadata.Statistics[i]` without bounds checks. A record with probes but no captured rows panics with index -1. Statistics or Values shorter than Probes also panic. This runs while `s.mu` is held, inside every Snapshot/poll call. A panic here crashes the presentation path, and if it is recovered upstream it can leave the mutex locked.
findings.suggestion: Before building readings, check that `len(record.rows) > 0`, `i < len(record.metadata.Statistics)` and `i < len(lastRow.Values)`. Skip the reading or leave `Value` at zero when the data is missing.

findings.title: Multiplicative perturbation is a no-op for zero values
findings.message: The test perturbs values multiplicatively. If `Points[0].Values[0]` or `Contributors[0].RMS[0]` is 0 in the fixture (common at a sweep start point), the value does not change. The test would then fail spuriously, and the failure would be misleading.
findings.suggestion: Assert that the value is non-zero before perturbing it, or use an additive perturbation that is significant relative to the record's tolerance.

findings.title: Benchmark ignores Wait result and measures an empty state
findings.message: The benchmark ignores whatever `s.Wait` returns. If the service never settles or the wait fails, the benchmark still runs. `revision` may then be stale, and the "unchanged" sub-benchmark would time full rebuilds instead of idle polls. The benchmark also never loads an example, so "full" measures an empty snapshot. Because of that it doesn't show a realistic cost gap between the two paths.
findings.suggestion: Check the result of `Wait`, for example `if err := s.Wait(b.Context()); err != nil { b.Fatal(err) }`. Load and pause an example circuit, as the test does, before reading the revision. Optionally assert in the "unchanged" loop that `changed` is false.

finding.title: Hard-coded limit in error message
finding.message: The "8 MiB" error message is hard-coded separately from `MaxResponseBytes`. It will drift the next time the limit changes, as the 1 MiB text nearly did here.
finding.suggestion: Build the message from the constant, e.g. `fmt.Sprintf("response exceeds %d MiB", MaxResponseBytes/(1024*1024))`.
